trade: Long, then flipped short · NY-AM · XFA · Loss, about -$768 (daily limit $500)
summary: Hard psychological day, written down so it never happens the same way again. You took a long about 5 minutes after the open on displacement with no deep retrace and not in a discount, it rejected off the EQ of the bullish leg and you lost about $300. From there you traded the P&L instead of the setup, stayed married to the weekly no-wick bias after the higher timeframe had flipped bullish, and ended about $768 down against a $500 daily limit.
good: You waited for the second 30-minute unfilled gap and got a clean rejection before the long re-entry, and your target (no-wick equal highs and London highs) was a real draw.
You walked away after the big loss instead of revenge trading further. You broke rules, but you stopped before it cost the account.
You were honest about it afterwards: "if I was focused on executing a good setup, I wouldn’t have executed the first trade."
fix: Broke: break-even at external highs. You put BE at internal liquidity (the 5-minute bearish unfill). AB: BE should have been the recent high that swept the London high.

Broke: bias matched the HTF narrative. The prior day put in a fat rejection wick taking out the lows, and price was about 400 points from the weekly no-wick low, so the HTF said longs. You stayed stuck on the bearish weekly idea.
Broke: traded the setup, not the P&L. After the first loss you were trading to make it back.

You closed a winning long to flip short on a weakness signal (bearish-leg OTE plus a 1-minute bearish gap plus an SMT at London high). Price went higher and later hit the Asia high, about $1,200 you left on the table.

questions.q: When the first loss hit (about $300), what would have stopped you from taking the next trade? Write the exact rule you want next time, in your words.

rule: When the HTF narrative flips, flip with it. Mark it in PRE MARKET before 9:30, and put BE at external highs/lows only.
notes: From Xavier’s own walkthrough on Oct 23, plus AB’s feedback.
